commitResults.messageBody: Move standard input and all user-facing output from Bob and TaskList into a dedicated Ui class. Return affected tasks from mark and unmark operations so TaskList remains responsible only for task state, while preserving the existing text interface and persistence behavior.

Move command splitting, task construction, index conversion, and date validation out of Bob into a dedicated Parser. Introduce ParsedCommand as an immutable representation of the command word and argument, leaving Bob responsible for coordinating UI, task-list, and storage operations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refine task status output and update documentation

commitResults.messageBody: Give Bob ownership of Ui, Parser, Storage, and TaskList, load saved tasks during construction, and move the command loop into run(). Keep main limited to selecting the default data path and starting the application. Include the accompanying parser comments and ParsedCommand getter documentation.

Keep Bob as the root application coordinator and move exception, parser, storage, task-domain, and UI classes into matching subpackages beneath src/main/java. Update package declarations and imports while preserving command behavior, persistence, and the source-root layout.

commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot locate tasks without scanning the entire task list.

Add a find command that performs case-insensitive description matching
and displays results in task order. Validate missing keywords and cover
matching behavior with parser and task-list tests.

Add sample task data for exercising keyword searches.

Implementation work can begin without making intended changes and risks
visible to the user.

Add a project-specific planning skill and require agents to present a
task-specific plan before editing. Reuse the existing Java standard for
documentation and coding requirements.

commitResults.messageTitle: Change names to enhance coding quality

commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce an FXML-based chat window so users can interact with Bob
through a graphical interface.

- Connect GUI input to Bob's command-processing logic
- Add styled dialog boxes and Bob's avatar
- Configure JavaFX for Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Preserve the command-line interface as an alternative entry point
- Ignore locally generated task data

Allow TaskList to be initialized from zero or more individual tasks while
retaining list-based construction for task collections loaded from storage.

Add tests for empty, single-task, and multiple-task varargs
construction.

Integrate varargs task-list construction and its focused tests into
master while retaining the branch boundary for the A-Varargs increment.

Rename command, search, dialog, and test identifiers so their purposes are clear and boolean names follow the required convention. Use arrow switch labels to express command branches without implicit fall-through.

Add Javadocs that describe the responsibilities, parameters, return values, and failure conditions of private helpers. Preserve existing AI-assistance attribution while replacing informal header comments.

Extract the minimum window dimensions into named constants and use the task status accessor consistently. Centralize task-number validation so all indexed operations enforce the same bounds without duplicated logic.

Task-list bookkeeping and JavaFX field injection rely on internal
assumptions that are not stated in code.

Undocumented assumptions make programming and FXML configuration errors
harder to identify near their source.

Add assertions for task-count consistency and required FXML-injected
controls. Keep user-input validation separate because assertions may be
disabled at runtime.
Document internal invariants with assertions

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Remove redundant task count state

commitResults.messageBody:
Task reconstruction mixes validation, status parsing, and creation.

This makes the storage format and happy path difficult to follow.

Extract focused helpers and name field positions to clarify each step.

Task status text is assembled through repeated string mutation.

This obscures the final representation and adds unnecessary steps.

Build the completion mark once and return the full string directly.

Avatar clipping repeats an unexplained numeric value three times.

A named constant makes the shared radius and center coordinates clear.

Automatic scrolling uses an unexplained numeric position.

Name the bottom position so the listener's intent is immediately clear.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Replace codes with descriptive enums
commitResults.messageBody:
Stored task records encode completion and task types as terse values.

Using raw codes at decision points hides their domain meaning.

Introduce enums that map storage codes to named domain values.

Rename the derived boolean to isTaskDone and switch on explicit task types.

Keep the serialized codes unchanged so existing data files remain valid.

executeParsedCommand mixed command dispatch with parsing, task updates, persistence, and response construction.

Extract focused handlers for state-changing and find commands. Centralize task-list persistence so the switch remains at one level of abstraction.

The constructor mixed dependency setup with task-loading recovery and
startup message construction. This obscured its high-level initialization
flow.

Extract stored-task loading into a focused operation and return its related
results together. Keep the constructor at one level of abstraction while
preserving loading behavior.

Deadline and event parsing mixed command dispatch, format validation, field
extraction, date conversion, and task creation. The mixed levels made each
parsing workflow difficult to scan.

Extract structured command details and date conversion into focused helpers.
Keep each task parser focused on assembling a task from validated values
while preserving validation messages and accepted formats.

Task persistence mixed directory preparation, file access, serialization,
and data-line parsing within its public operations. This made storage
workflows depend on low-level details.

Extract directory creation, task writing, and line conversion into focused
helpers. Keep the public methods responsible for coordinating storage and
translating I/O failures into domain errors.

The JavaFX start method mixed application startup with FXML wiring and
detailed stage configuration. This hid the main startup sequence among
framework operations.

Extract window loading and stage display into focused helpers. Keep start at
a single orchestration level while preserving the controller setup and
window dimensions.

The controller lifecycle and command handler mixed orchestration with FXML
invariant checks and dialog-container manipulation. These details distracted
from each method's intent.

Extract FXML checks, automatic scrolling, and message display into focused
helpers. Keep assertions as invariant documentation and preserve the existing
command submission behavior.

Dialog construction and factory methods mixed object creation with FXML
loading, injection checks, and detailed visual configuration. This obscured
the intent of each creation path.

Extract layout loading, invariant checks, and user or Bob presentation into
focused helpers. Keep the factories at a single level of abstraction without
changing dialog appearance.

Deadline and event validation combined array-length checks, repeated
normalization, and missing-value checks in compound expressions. This made
the validation rules difficult to identify at a glance.

Name each validation condition and normalize extracted values once. Validate
array lengths before accessing their elements to keep the parsing flow clear
and safe without changing accepted formats or error messages.

Command-specific parsing helpers were separated from the methods that use
them. Readers had to move between unrelated sections to follow deadline and
event parsing.

Place each detail-extraction helper directly after its corresponding task
parser. Keep shared validation and date conversion after the command-specific
workflows so the class reads from specialized operations to shared utilities.

Private save helpers separated the two public storage operations. This made
the class interface harder to scan before reaching its implementation details.

Place saveTasks and loadTasks together after construction, followed by private
helpers grouped by their save and load workflows. Preserve all persistence and
error-handling behavior.

deleteTask appeared after the task query methods even though it changes the
same collection as addTask, markTask, and unmarkTask. This separated related
operations and interrupted the class's logical grouping.

Move deleteTask beside the other task mutations and keep read-only queries in
the following section. Preserve every method implementation and behavior.

Private initialization helpers separated the controller's FXML lifecycle and
event-handler methods. This made the operations invoked by JavaFX harder to
scan as a group.

Place initialize, setBob, and submitUserCommand before the private view
helpers. Preserve the existing call sequence and user-interface behavior.

Private construction details appeared before the public factory methods that
form the class interface. Readers encountered FXML machinery before learning
how dialog boxes are created.

Place the user and Bob dialog factories before private construction and
configuration helpers. Preserve all factory behavior and visual styling.

The task-loading loop nested exception handling around its normal parsing and
collection update. This interrupted the successful path with error-reporting
details.

Move line-specific exception translation into a focused helper. Keep the loop
as a direct sequence of identifying, parsing, and adding each stored task while
preserving the existing error message and line number.
Update code quality to master

commitResults.messageTitle: TaskList: Use stream to find tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Finding tasks manually accumulated matching elements in a loop. The operation
is a direct collection filter, so the loop obscured that intent.

Use a stream filter and collect matches into a new ArrayList. Preserve the
display order and the existing mutable, independent return value.
